acceptance: Composite-key tables keep the full key or raise; executed Doris/StarRocks tests insert duplicate-prefix rows and assert row counts.
Behavior documented in the fork README; fork PR merged; adoption via the next wheel.
Published Doris/StarRocks results using unique/primary table models listed for rerun review.
description: Adversarial review H3: transpile_ddl with key_columns=(l_orderkey,l_linenumber) writes UNIQUE KEY (l_orderkey) for table_model=unique and DUPLICATE KEY (l_orderkey) for primary (ddl_engines.py:247-277 fall back to the first keyable column); legacy doris.py:861-870 is identical. A unique key narrower than the real key keeps one row per l_orderkey, so most lineitem rows are lost (inferred; not executed on Doris). Fix in the fork: raise when key columns are not a leading prefix of the column list (or reorder columns), never narrow the key; execute on the Doris and StarRocks CI jobs with a composite key and row-count assertions. BenchBox published Doris/StarRocks results using table_model unique must be checked.
